storyTagline: A record season on the ground, a second straight title in Atlanta won with key pieces missing time, and two new names in the Hall of Fame.

stories.headline: Atlanta Does It Again
stories.dek: The Falcons went 13-3-1 and held off the Broncos 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII, carried by a record season from Ryland Maxwell and two first-year players who left with rings.

stories.headline: Maxwell Runs Into the Record Book
stories.dek: 2,272 rushing yards in one season, a Super Bowl MVP and a fourth ring before his hundredth game.

stories.headline: A Title Won Short-Handed
stories.dek: Orlando Larienne played 15 of Atlanta's 20 games and Vyncint Heath played 18. The champions won anyway.

stories.headline: Green Bay Finds Its Back
stories.dek: Angelo Moton ran for 1,717 yards and 31 touchdowns and was named Rookie of the Year for the Packers.

stories.headline: Two for the Hall: Sawyer and Horsted
stories.dek: A back who keeps running for the Jets and a Rams safety who never left Los Angeles both crossed Career Legacy 7,000.

stories.headline: Record Watch: A Dead Heat for Second
stories.dek: Von Horsted caught Dan Mosley at 2,658 career tackles, 204 short of Mose Junior, with K'Lavon Settle closing behind them.

stories.headline: Long Careers, Late Introductions
stories.dek: Vic Cannon in Los Angeles, Terron Stidham in Baltimore and Marvell Rodgers in Tennessee joined the card pool with decades of work already behind them.

stories.headline: The Jets Hand the Ball to a Rookie
stories.dek: Jimmy Tillery threw 589 passes in his first season and was intercepted 4 times. Ty Lock, the old starter, is a Giant now.

stories.headline: Life After Atlanta
stories.dek: Brandon Jaclyde, Shareef London and Perrion Randall left the champions after one season. All three spent Y84 watching their old club win again.

stories.headline: Denver Meets Skura, and Loses, Again
stories.dek: Four Super Bowls against the Broncos, four wins, with three different clubs across 68 seasons.
